🧱 Battlemap Builder

"Ten-foot corridor. No, ten. That's five. Here, I'll just draw it."

Draw your own battle map on a 5-foot grid: paint the floors, draw the walls, and put down doors, stairs, and furniture. Everything saves in your browser as you draw. Then press 🎲 Play to run the fight on it, with tokens, fog of war, and a Player View for the TV. Or share a link, download a PNG for your virtual tabletop, or print it at 1 inch = 5 feet for miniatures.

🧱 Battlemap 🌍 World Map
⚔️ Initiative Tracker

🖌️ Floor

Walls draw themselves wherever floor meets bare rock. Right-click or hold Shift to paint bare rock back. Fill stops at walls you've drawn.

🧱 Walls

Drag along the grid lines to draw a wall, or click one grid line to put a wall on it or take it off. Right-drag or Shift-drag rubs walls out.

You only need walls inside a floor: between two rooms, or to split a hall. Its outline draws itself.

🚪 Doors and stairs

Doors go on the grid line nearest the pointer, across a corridor or a gap in a wall. A new door put on an old one replaces it. Stairs and trapdoors fill a square. Hold Alt to put one anywhere.

🪑 Furniture

R turns it 90° before you put it down (Shift+R the other way, Alt+R 15°). It snaps to the grid; hold Alt to put it anywhere. Resize it with 👆 Select.

🔢 Labels

Click to number a room or mark a spot. It goes in the middle of the square; Alt puts it right where you click. Leave labels off a players' copy when you download or print.

R turn 90° (Shift+R back, Alt+R 15°) · drag the square handle to resize (Shift keeps its shape) and the round one to turn (Alt: any angle) · arrow keys move it a square (Alt: a little) · Ctrl+D duplicate · Delete remove · Esc let go.

🧽 Erase

📏 Ruler

Drag from one square to another. It measures from square middles; hold Alt to measure from exactly where you click. Esc clears it.

⚔️ In the fight

➕ A token of your own

For an ally, a bystander, or a marker that isn't in the fight. A token of your own shows its name to the players; a monster from the fight stays an unknown creature until you reveal it in the tracker.

N next turn (Shift+N back) · arrow keys move the picked-up token a square · Delete takes it off · Esc lets go.

☁️ Fog of war

Click to reveal; right-click or hold Shift to hide again. 🚪 Room reveals a whole room or corridor at a click, out to its walls and doors. The shaded squares are hidden from the players: they see them black.

✋ Pan

Drag to move around the map. With any tool, hold Space or the middle mouse button and drag. Ctrl + mouse wheel zooms.

🗺️ Take it to the table

Your maps are kept in this browser only, up to 30 of them, saved as you draw (💾 Back up everything). 🔗 Copy Link puts the whole map in the link, so whoever opens it gets their own copy to change. Roll a dungeon on the Worldbuilder's Sites tab and press ✏️ Edit in the Battlemap Builder to open it here with its floors, doors, furniture, and room numbers already in place. The floor, furniture, door, and token pictures are the Gazette's own. Blocked pop-ups? The Player View opens from this link too.

How the Battlemap Builder works

The map is a grid of 5-foot squares, up to 60 by 60 (300 by 300 feet). Paint floor where the rooms and corridors go and the walls draw themselves around them. Then draw walls where two rooms meet, put doors in the gaps, and furnish the rooms. 🎨 Illustrated draws painted floors and doors; ✒️ Classic ink draws flat floors and inked walls and doors, like the Sites tab's classic maps.

Tools

  • 🖌️ Floor (B): brush, box, or fill, in fourteen floors, from flagstones and carpet to ice and lava.
  • 🧱 Walls (W): drag along the grid lines, or click one line to toggle it.
  • 🚪 Doors (D) and 🪑 Furniture (P): doors snap to the grid lines, furniture to the squares. Hold Alt to put either anywhere, at any angle.
  • 🔢 Labels (L): room numbers that count up as you click.
  • 👆 Select (V): move, turn, resize, duplicate, or delete a door, piece of furniture, or label.
  • 🧽 Erase (E), 📏 Ruler (M), and ✋ Pan (H). Ctrl+Z undoes, Ctrl+Y redoes.

🎲 Play mode: run the fight on the map

For a game around one table with a TV or a second screen. Press 🎲 Play above the tools and the map starts hidden under fog of war.

  • 👆 Tokens (V): the fight in the Initiative Tracker shows up beside the map. Add the party, an encounter, or Bestiary monsters there, then put each one down with 📍, or all of them at once. Monsters come in at their size (a Large ogre takes 2 × 2 squares) with a picture of their creature type, and characters with their class. A token of your own covers an ally, a bystander, or a marker. Drag a token and the ruler counts the feet.
  • Each token from the fight shows its hit points and conditions as the tracker has them, and a ring marks whose turn it is. ▶ Next turn (N) moves the tracker's turn on from here.
  • ☁️ Fog (F): click a room to reveal it out to its walls and doors, or drag a box, or paint square by square. Right-click or Shift hides it again.
  • 📺 Player View opens a window to drag onto the TV: the map with everything unrevealed in black, the tokens the players can see, whose turn it is, and your ruler while you measure. Secret doors, tokens you hide (🙈), and hit points never reach it, and monsters stay "Unknown" until you reveal them in the tracker. It frames what they've seen so far, or the whole map.

At the table

  • For a virtual tabletop, download the PNG at the grid size it uses (70 pixels for Roll20, 100 for Foundry) and it lines up with the VTT's own grid. Leave the labels and secret doors off for the players' copy.
  • For miniatures, print at 1 inch = 5 feet. A big map comes out on several pages: tape them together by the page numbers.
  • The ruler counts every diagonal as 5 feet, the 5e rule, or 5-10-5 if your table plays the variant.

Works with

The Worldbuilder's Sites tab rolls a keyed dungeon and sends its map here to finish by hand. Build the fights in its rooms with the Toolbox's Encounter Builder, then run them here in 🎲 Play mode alongside the Initiative Tracker.
